description:
FOUND s493 (Fable, 2026-09-20) by the DEPARSE MUTATION run: every battery program re-spelled by `perl -MO=Deparse[,-p]`, the re-spelling VALIDATED by perl (same stdout + rc), then run under PCL.  Of 77 programs PCL gets right as written, 21 (25 with -p) go wrong re-spelled; these two shapes explain 13 + 5 of them (corpus: ~/pcl-agent-scratch/s493/corpus/{orig,dp,dpp}, runner bin/diffrun.pl + bin/mkvariants.pl + corpus/cmpvar.pl).

    my(@hs) = @{$hr;}{'a', 'b'};     push @{$dept{$r{'dept'}};}, \%r;     *{$AUTOLOAD;} = sub {...};     printf {$o;} "%s\n", 'x';
        perl: fine (a deref block is a BLOCK; `;` is legal in it)     PCL: "statement dropped ... Missing case: ['Token::Symbol<$hr>','Token::Structure<;>']"
    print "/tmp/x.${$}.tmp\n";        perl: the pid                   PCL: crash, "The variable $} is unbound"

Humans write the first rarely (`@{ my $r = f(); $r }` does occur; generators and Deparse always) and the second OFTEN -- `"${$}"` is how `$$` is delimited from following text in a string.  Fix shapes: (1) a cast block's content is a STATEMENT LIST whose value is its last statement -- at minimum strip a trailing null statement, properly lower it like a `do` block (find the existing `${ \ ... }` / `@{[ ... ]}` handling and route through it, rule 11); (2) InterpScan: `${` followed by a PUNCTUATION variable name and `}` is that variable (`${$}`, `${!}`, `${@}`, `${0}`, `${^W}` is already special) -- Pl/InterpScan.pm only (standing rule §8), and the CODE-side spelling `${$}` too.
WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THE TWO SHAPES: Deparse is a free, perl-validated SPELLING MUTATOR for any corpus (see the s493 write-up); these two shapes are what currently blinds it.  Behind them the run found the known non-leading `local` family (#1192/#1243: `(local $g = 2);` is never restored) and nothing else new on this corpus.
subject: Two spellings B::Deparse always writes and PCL cannot read: a deref/handle BLOCK with a statement terminator `@{$x;}` / `*{$AUTOLOAD;}` / `printf {$fh;} ...` (whole-statement DROP) and `"${$}"` in a string (= `$$`; read as the variable `$}` => crash "The variable $} is unbound")
